notes.zones: Differences between zones come from long-term precipitation patterns (PRISM), mostly elevation. Nothing measures snow by zone.
notes.wind: Days 1 to 3 include wind loading: more snow on slopes just over a ridge from the wind, less on the exposed side. Its strength is tuned to one skier's account of where Vail loads up (about 13 in in the lee when the base amount is 10). Nothing measures it.
notes.sun: Sun effects are modelled and unchecked.
notes.first_chair: The ranking's weights are choices, not fitted values: nothing records where the skiing was best. Zone amounts differ mostly by elevation.
notes.analogs: Shown for context. On held-out days the average of the closest past days missed by more than the model did.
notes.water: Mid-mountain water, 24 h ahead: typical miss 0.06 in over 1,420 held-out days (2018 to 2026). Level with the National Blend of Models.
notes.settled: Settled depth is checked against seven SNOTEL depth sensors: typical miss 1.7 in on snow days.
notes.big_days: Big days are under-called by the median. When the setup looks good, read the high end of the range.
notes.gusts: Ridge gusts are checked at Copper Mountain summit airport station (12,075 ft, 20 km away): the day's peak gust in lift hours missed by 6 mph on average over 1,064 days.
notes.lifts: Checked at the summit station only: days called likely to reach 40 mph did so 65% of the time, possible 29%, low 3%. Each lift's share of the ridge gust and the hold thresholds are assumptions; no record of holds is public.
